list.name: datasource
list.label: Data source
list.description: VictoriaMetrics holds the full history. Prometheus only keeps 15d, so any range beyond that must use VictoriaMetrics.

list.name: tariff
list.label: Tariff (£/kWh)
list.description: Actual unit rate, 25.06p/kWh. UNIT RATE ONLY — the standing charge is deliberately excluded, so these figures are the marginal cost of running this host, not a line off the bill. Update when the tariff changes.

list.name: baseline_w
list.label: Assumed non-CPU baseline (W)
list.description: Everything RAPL cannot see: panel, both disks, fans, chipset, WiFi, PSU conversion loss. Derived from Notebookcheck's measurements of this exact model (Inspiron 17-5770 / i5-8250U / FHD): 4.08W wall at idle minimum brightness, of which ~2.9W is non-CPU, plus ~0.7W WiFi and ~1.3W for the HDD that SeaweedFS and VictoriaMetrics keep spinning. Still an inference from someone else's wall meter, not a measurement of THIS host — a metering plug would replace it outright. Raise it towards 9W if the backlight ever goes back to full.

list.name: scrape_s
list.label: Scrape interval (s)
list.description: Seconds per sample, used to convert a sample count into observed seconds so the baseline is charged only for time actually observed. Must match the Prometheus scrapeInterval (30s at time of writing) — if that changes and this does not, every energy and cost figure scales wrong by the same ratio.

panels.title: What this dashboard does and does not measure

options.content:
The **Measured** row is real: Intel RAPL counters for the CPU package and DRAM.

The **Estimated** row is *not* metered wall power. RAPL cannot see the display panel, either disk, fans, chipset, WiFi, or the charger's AC/DC conversion loss — on this Inspiron 5770 that is most of the actual draw. Those panels add the `baseline_w` variable to the measured CPU figure to approximate whole-system power. **The cost numbers are only as good as that assumption.** For true cost, meter the wall socket and repoint these panels at it.

`baseline_w` is not a guess pulled from the air: it is derived from Notebookcheck's wall measurements of this exact model (4.08 W idle at minimum brightness, 9.6 W at maximum), adjusted for WiFi and a permanently-spinning HDD. Expect ~7.6 W total, inside the measured 4.08–9.6 W band. Cost uses the **unit rate only** — the standing charge is out of scope, so this is the marginal cost of running the host, not a bill line.

**Gaps and outages:** every energy figure covers only the *observed* portion of the selected range — the baseline is charged per sample actually recorded, not per wall-clock second, so downtime is not silently billed. Check **Data coverage** first: below 100% means part of the window is missing and the totals are correspondingly partial. One caveat that cannot be worked around here — the RAPL counter wraps roughly every 34h at idle, so a monitoring gap longer than that loses a whole 72.8 Wh wrap and undercounts CPU energy.

panels.title: CPU package power
panels.description: Live CPU package draw, averaged over 5m. This is measured, not estimated.

panels.title: CPU energy over range
panels.description: increase() of the package joules counter across the dashboard time range, converted to kWh. Counter wraps at max_energy_range_uj are handled by increase().

panels.title: Data coverage
panels.description: Fraction of the selected range that actually has samples. Anything below 100% means an outage, a monitoring gap, or a range extending before this data existed — in all of those cases the energy and cost figures below cover only the observed portion. Read this before trusting any number on this dashboard.

panels.title: Power by RAPL zone
panels.description: core, uncore and dram are components INSIDE package — do not sum them with it, that double-counts. psys is deliberately omitted: it reports ~0.08 W against a ~2.5 W package on this chip, i.e. it is non-functional here rather than a whole-SoC superset.

panels.title: Estimated — whole system and cost (uses assumed baseline)
Estimated total power
panels.description: Measured CPU package power plus the assumed non-CPU baseline. Estimate, not metered.

panels.title: Estimated energy over range
panels.description: (measured CPU joules + baseline watts x OBSERVED seconds) converted to kWh. Observed seconds is the sample count times the scrape interval, not the wall-clock range — so an outage or monitoring gap is excluded from the baseline rather than silently billed. Check the Data coverage panel alongside this.

panels.title: Estimated cost over range
panels.description: Estimated energy over the selected range x the tariff variable. Only as accurate as the assumed baseline, and only covers the OBSERVED portion of the range — if Data coverage is below 100%, this is the cost of the time that was recorded, not of the whole window.

panels.title: Estimated cost per month
panels.description: Projection, not a measurement: average power across the OBSERVED portion of the range, extrapolated to a 730h month of continuous running. Dividing by observed rather than wall-clock seconds is deliberate — it answers 'what would a month at this running rate cost', so a mid-range outage does not drag the figure down and make the host look cheaper than it is. It therefore assumes 24/7 operation going forward. A short or unrepresentative range still misleads: select at least 24h.

panels.title: Estimated total power over time
panels.description: Measured CPU package power plus the flat assumed baseline. The shape is real; the offset is assumed.
